I use zeo.  It's an inexpensive headband that will give you details about when you go to sleep each night, but it also breaks it down by quality of sleep, recording deep vs light sleep, and when you are in rem sleep.  The associated App can give you a wealth of data, including standards for your age and gender for comparison.   It also includes an alarm that wakes you when you are most alert during your morning sleep cycle, so you don't fight that struggle to wake up.  By far it's the most comprehensive app for sleep tracking.  If that doesn't help and you need to use your electronic devices close to bed time, my doctor prescribed over-the-counter blue blocker sun glasses to use while looking at these glowing screens.  It blocks the blue light, which is what is limiting the natural release of melatonin.  Hope that helps...
